legend: You are creating a tour of the Peak District hills for a friend visiting from the Netherlands. The walk will go from the locally famous viewpoint "Hill 1" to the world-famous viewpoint "Hill 2".
To make this friend feel at home, you want to minimise the difference in height between the highest and lowest hills of the walk.
Given a graph of the local points of interest and paths between them, find such an optimally-flat route.
input: One line containing the number of hills, n%%ZSMJ0%% (2≤n≤5000%%ZSMJ1%%), and the number of trails connecting them, m%%ZSMJ2%% (1≤m≤25000%%ZSMJ3%%).
One line containing n%%ZSMJ4%% integers h1…hn%%ZSMJ5%% (0≤h≤106%%ZSMJ6%%), the heights in metres of the hills from 1%%ZSMJ7%% to n%%ZSMJ8%%.

m%%ZSMJ9%% further lines, the i%%ZSMJ10%%-th of which contains two integers a%%ZSMJ11%% and b%%ZSMJ12%% (1≤a,b≤n%%ZSMJ13%%) indicating that there is a bi-directional path between hills a%%ZSMJ14%% and b%%ZSMJ15%%.
It is guaranteed that there is a path (direct or indirect) between hills 1%%ZSMJ16%% and 2%%ZSMJ17%%.
output: Output the minimum possible distance between the maximum and minimum heights of hills encountered on a walk between hills 1%%ZSMJ18%% and 2%%ZSMJ19%%.
